questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop people stealing from shops and offices
How honest people really are, especially with money
The life of Benjamin Franklin and his famous sayings
Why small businesses are closing in the UK
questions.why: Rob says they're talking about honesty and how honest people are, particularly when spending money.

options: A sales assistant checks what you pay
You pay with a card at a machine
You get a discount for being honest
You put in the money yourself and nobody checks
questions.why: Neil says you put money in a box, but it's up to you to put in the right amount.

questions.q: Why might a small business use an honesty box?
options: So it doesn't need a sales assistant
Because customers prefer it
To make more profit
Because the law requires it
questions.why: Neil says it means you don't need a sales assistant.

questions.q: What does Rob mean when he says 'Honestly, Neil!' about the quiz?
options: He is promising to tell Neil the whole truth
He doesn't know the answer and wants a clue
He is annoyed because the question is too easy
He thinks Neil has cheated by looking it up
questions.why: Rob says everyone will know the answer, and Neil explains 'honestly' can show irritation.

questions.q: According to Philip Graves, are most people honest?
options: Yes, almost everyone is
Only when they are shopping
No, they aren't
Only people in small social groups
questions.why: He asks 'Are most people honest?' and says 'the answer to that is no'.

questions.q: Why does Philip Graves say humans developed the ability to be dishonest?
options: Getting an advantage over others helped us survive
It helped us make more friends in our groups
It was taught to us by our parents as children
It made groups work together better when hunting
questions.why: He says if we can gain an advantage over people around us, we have a greater chance of surviving.

questions.q: What stops people being dishonest all the time, according to Philip Graves?
options: Fear of the police
Religious rules
Not having enough chances to cheat
The risk of being pushed out of the group
questions.why: He says we balance helping ourselves against 'the risk of being ostracised by the group'.

questions.q: Why does Rob think we value honesty?
options: Dishonest people always get caught and punished in the end
Selfish behaviour is disliked and societies work better
Honest people earn more money during their careers
Being honest is much easier than remembering lies
questions.why: Rob says others won't like selfish behaviour, and societies work better when people co-operate.
